screening.reason: Analyses ABIDE-I resting-state functional connectivity (vertex-wise, C-PAC pipeline) for a group-difference (ASD vs NT) analysis; meets inclusion 2-3.

evidence_spans.text: We studied 211 males from three sites of the ABIDE-I dataset comprising 103 participants with an ASD diagnosis (mean ± SD age = 20.8 ± 8.1 years) and 108 neurotypical controls (NT, 19.2 ± 7.2 years).
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort was 211 males (103 ASD, 108 NT) from three ABIDE-I sites.

evidence_spans.text: Compared to NT, ASD participants presented with widespread reductions in CD, generally indicating shorter average connection length and thus suggesting reduced long-range connectivity but increased short-range connections.
evidence_spans.claim: Main finding: ASD shows widespread connectivity-distance reductions, implying relatively reduced long-range and increased short-range connectivity.

evidence_spans.text: included imaging and  clinical data from three different sites that included data  from > = 10 ASD and NT respectively, i.e., University of  Pittsburgh School of Medicine (PITT), New York Univer­ sity Langone Medical Center (NYU), and University of  Utah School of Medicine (USM).
evidence_spans.claim: Three ABIDE-I sites were used: PITT, NYU, USM.

evidence_spans.text: After excluding cases with high  head motion (cutoff: >2SD over mean framewise dis­ placement, n = 10), we obtained a sample size of n = 211  (103/108 ASD/NT).
evidence_spans.claim: A motion-based exclusion rule (>2 SD above mean FD) removed 10 subjects to reach n=211.

evidence_spans.text: based on  the configurable pipeline for the analysis of connectomes  (C-PAC) (https://fcp-indi.github.io/) [83], including slice- time and head motion correction, skull stripping and  intensity normalization.
Subjects with a mean framewise displacement  (FD) > 0.3 mm in rs-fMRI (two SD from the mean across  all subjects) were excluded (n = 9).
evidence_spans.claim: An additional rs-fMRI-specific FD>0.3mm exclusion removed 9 subjects.

evidence_spans.text: Data were harmo­ nized for site effects while preserving effects of age and  ASD diagnosis using ComBat [86]
evidence_spans.claim: Site effects were handled using ComBat harmonization.

evidence_spans.text: Effect sizes dif­ fered across seven intrinsic functional networks [21],  with higher effects towards transmodal compared to  sensory/motor networks and peak reductions in CD in  the limbic network (Cohen's d=-0.159, Fig.  3A).
evidence_spans.claim: Peak effect size for CD reduction was in the limbic network (Cohen's d = -0.159).

assessments.support: Site, N, ADOS-based diagnosis and motion exclusion thresholds explicitly stated.
Table 1 gives age, IQ, ADOS by group; three named sites.
C-PAC pipeline with motion correction, CompCor, band-pass filter, no-GSR with GSR control analysis described in detail.
In-person diagnostic interview using ADOS described.
Age, head motion and site included as covariates/handled via ComBat; study restricted to males due to ABIDE-I female sparsity.
ComBat harmonization for site; motion exclusion thresholds applied; model CDi = ß0+ß1*Age+ß2*Diagnosis+ß3*Head Motion.
Connectivity distance derived from vertex-wise FC and geodesic distance mapping, a previously published approach.
Random field theory correction and FDR correction described for vertex-wise and cluster-wise tests.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-documented cohort, pipeline, confound handling (ComBat, motion exclusion) and multiple-comparison correction for this associational analysis; main limitation is restriction to males and 3 of 17 ABIDE-I sites, explicitly acknowledged.

charting.title: Contracted functional connectivity profiles in autism

charting.specific_features: Vertex-wise intra-hemispheric functional connectivity combined with cortical surface geodesic distance to derive connectivity distance (CD)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC pipeline; Connectome Workbench; HCP pipelines; Conte69 surface template
charting.feature_change_direction: Widespread reductions in connectivity distance (CD) in ASD vs NT, peaking in transmodal/paralimbic systems and the limbic intrinsic network
charting.summary_key_findings: ASD showed widespread reductions in connectivity distance relative to NT, concentrated in heteromodal/paralimbic transmodal cortex, interpreted as relatively shorter long-range and more short-range connectivity; CD reductions correlated with IQ but not with age or ADOS severity.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) analysis; ABIDE-I; n=211 males (103 ASD, 108 NT) from PITT, NYU, USM.
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI mapped to Conte69 cortical surface; vertex-wise functional connectivity combined with geodesic distance to derive connectivity distance (CD); ComBat site harmonization; vertex-wise t-tests with random field theory correction.
narrative_row.outcomes: Widespread CD reductions in ASD vs NT concentrated in transmodal/paralimbic cortex, peak effect in the limbic intrinsic network (Cohen's d=-0.159); CD correlated positively with IQ but not age or ADOS severity.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Restricted to 3 of 17 ABIDE-I sites and to males only; cross-sectional; heterogeneity in autism limits generalizability (authors' own limitation).
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a novel connectivity-distance (geodesic-weighted FC) derivative of ABIDE-I rs-fMRI, with explicit, reconstructible site/exclusion rules but no participant list.

kg_link.cohort_description: Three ABIDE-I sites (PITT, NYU, USM), males only, ADOS-confirmed ASD, excluded for high head motion (>2SD mean FD, n=10) and rs-fMRI FD>0.3mm (n=9); final n=211 (103 ASD/108 NT).
kg_link.pipeline: C-PAC (slice-time/motion correction, CompCor, band-pass 0.01-0.1Hz, no GSR; ComBat site harmonization)
kg_link.atlas: Conte69 surface template (vertex-wise, no ROI atlas)
kg_link.finding: ASD showed widespread reductions in connectivity distance (shorter average functional connection length) vs NT, peaking in transmodal/paralimbic cortex and the limbic intrinsic network (Cohen's d=-0.159).
evidence_quotes: We studied 211 males from three sites of the ABIDE-I dataset comprising 103 participants with an ASD  diagnosis (mean ± SD age = 20.8 ± 8.1 years) and 108 neurotypical controls (NT, 19.2 ± 7.2 years).

Compared to NT, ASD participants presented with widespread reductions in CD, generally indicating  shorter average connection length and thus suggesting reduced long-range connectivity but increased short- range connections.
